acceptanceCriteria: Given a return-trip order with a promo code applied, when the Mozio email confirmation is generated, then the return trip section must display the promo code discount amount in the same format and position as the outbound trip section.
Given a return-trip order with a promo code applied to both outbound and return legs, the email confirmation must show the promo discount amount for each leg independently.

Given a return-trip order with a promo code applied only to the return leg, the email confirmation must show the promo discount amount for the return leg and not display a promo line for the outbound leg.
Given a return-trip order with a fixed-amount promo code, the email must display the exact discounted currency amount for the return trip.
Given a return-trip order with a percentage-based promo code, the email must display the calculated discount amount for the return trip.
The outbound trip promo discount display must remain unchanged and correct after the fix (no regression).

acceptanceCriteria: Given a return-trip order with a promo code applied, when the Mozio dispatch report is built, the return-trip dispatch must include report.price.discount with the correct amount and currency matching the return leg's discount.

Given a return-trip order with a promo code applied to both outbound and return legs, each dispatch in the Mozio submit payload must contain its own independent report.price.discount reflecting that leg's promo amount.

Given a return-trip order with a promo code applied only to the return leg, the return-trip dispatch must include report.price.discount and the outbound dispatch must have no discount field (or undefined).
Given a return-trip order with a fixed-amount promo code, the return-trip dispatch report.price.discount.amount.value must equal the exact discounted currency amount for the return leg.
Given a return-trip order with a percentage-based promo code, the return-trip dispatch report.price.discount.amount.value must equal the calculated discount amount for the return leg.
The outbound trip promo discount display in the Mozio email confirmation must remain unchanged and correct after the fix (no regression).

The sanitized dispatch report payload used for logging must include the discount amount and name for both outbound and return dispatches when a promo code is applied, without dropping or zeroing the return-trip discount.
after.description: [Mozio] - The Promo code amount is NOT displayed as expected for Return trip tickets in the Mozio email confirmation. The root cause is that when building the Mozio dispatch report for return-trip tickets, the discount amount is not correctly computed or propagated, resulting in the promo code discount being missing or zeroed in the email confirmation for the return leg.
after.title: [Mozio] - Promo code discount amount missing/incorrect for return-trip tickets in Mozio email confirmation dispatch report

Given a return-trip order with a promo code applied, the outbound dispatch report.price.discount must remain identical to the value produced before the return-trip discount fix (no regression).

notes: Modified AC3 to remove the ambiguous '(or undefined)' — a field either exists or it doesn't; specifying both makes the criterion untestable since two different outcomes would pass. Modified AC6 to replace 'unchanged and correct' with a regression-specific formulation referencing the pre-fix baseline value, making it verifiable by comparing against a known snapshot. Added AC8 (no-promo baseline) to ensure the absence path is explicitly covered — without it, a change that always adds a discount field would pass all original ACs. Added AC9 (currency consistency) because AC1 mentions currency but AC4/AC5 don't, creating a gap where a fixed or percentage promo could propagate the wrong currency on the return leg. Added AC10 (rounding precision) as an edge case for fractional-cent discounts that could cause downstream display or reconciliation failures.
